stem: In a game repeated a KNOWN finite number of times, how do players treat the last period?
choices: As a one-shot game, since no one can be punished afterward

stem: According to the slides, finite repeated games:
choices: Always collapse back to a one-shot simultaneous game

stem: Why does a player have an incentive to break a promise in the second-to-last period of a finitely repeated game?
choices: There is no effective punishment in the last period, because both defect then anyway
The rival cannot see the move
The payoffs are larger in that period

stem: True or false: In a prisoner's dilemma repeated exactly 100 times with a known end, firms should cooperate in the first 99 periods and cheat only in the last.
explain: False. Backward induction unravels cooperation from period 100 all the way back to period 1.

stem: Cooperation can survive in a finitely repeated game when:
choices: Players do not know when the game will end
Payoffs are listed in a tree
The last period is announced in advance
explain: With an uncertain end there is always a chance of future punishment (textbook).

stem: True or false: The unraveling argument for finitely repeated games uses backward induction, starting from the final period.
explain: True. Solve the last period first, then step back.

stem: Your only rival announces it will close its store in two weeks. You have kept prices high together for years. What does game theory predict?
choices: Collusion breaks down now, since the game has a known end
Prices stay high until the rival closes
explain: Like Comprehension Quiz 9 Q7: a known final period removes the threat of punishment.

stem: An employee has announced she will retire in three weeks. Why might her effort drop?
choices: She has a dominant strategy to work
The end-of-period problem: there is no future relationship to protect
explain: The textbook's end-of-period problem. Firms respond with things like retirement bonuses or references.

stem: A tourist-area street vendor will never see a customer again. Which statement fits?
choices: This is an infinitely repeated game
The vendor will always sell high quality
The vendor has an incentive to sell low-quality goods, since there is no repeat business to lose
Customers can punish the vendor next period
explain: One-shot interactions remove the reputation incentive.

stem: How could a firm reduce the end-of-period problem with a worker who will leave in a year?
choices: Pay part of compensation as a bonus at the end, or make future references depend on performance
Announce the exact last day to everyone
explain: Making something depend on the last periods keeps a future reward in play.

stem: Gas stations A and B will compete for exactly 10 weeks before a highway bypass closes their road. Each week's game is a prisoner's dilemma with a unique Nash equilibrium (both price low). What happens in week 1?
choices: Both price high, then low in week 10
explain: Week 10 is one-shot, so both price low; then week 9 has nothing to protect, and so on back to week 1.

stem: Which change would make collusion between two firms easier to sustain?
choices: The game is played only once
One firm says it will exit next month
The firms are unsure when their competition will end
A regulator announces the market will close on a fixed date
explain: Uncertain end = always a chance of future punishment.

stem: True or false: Visa and Mastercard playing the fee game for exactly two periods would both lower fees in both periods.
explain: True (slides p. 28). The second period is one-shot; the first has no effective punishment.

stem: What condition makes a finitely repeated game unravel to the one-shot outcome in every period?
choices: The final period is known and the one-shot game has a unique Nash equilibrium
explain: Both conditions are needed for the backward-induction argument.

stem: Each year there is a 10% chance that a new law ends two firms' market. Compared with a market that ends on a known date, collusion is:
choices: Easier to sustain, since every period may be followed by another
explain: An uncertain end works like an infinite horizon with extra discounting (textbook).
